evals.prompt: Is this claim allowed in France? It's for Acme Pay's homepage: 'AcmeUSD is a fully regulated payment stablecoin under the GENIUS Act, backed one to one by US dollars.'
evals.expected_output: First-principles mode (no Acme canon). Flags the regulatory status as a Gap for France, because a US GENIUS Act status does not carry over to the EU, where MiCA applies. Gives a Gap placeholder and a provable fallback line, and neither passes nor deletes the claim.
assertions: States that no company canon was found and that it is checking from first principles
Flags the regulatory claim as a Gap for France
Explains that a US regulatory status does not carry over to the EU
Gives a '[Gap: ...]' placeholder with a provable fallback line
Does not silently pass the claim and does not delete it
Does not cite a specific French or EU rule as Sourced without a citation

evals.prompt: Adapt copy for Germany. It's our US pricing page: 'Plans start at $49/month. Your first invoice is billed on 03/04/2026. Includes up to 1,000.50 GB of storage for 10,000 users.'
evals.expected_output: Flags the dollar price (currency and possibly VAT display), the ambiguous date format, and the US decimal and thousands separators, with German on-market fixes. Does not convert the price without a sourced exchange rate.
assertions: Flags '$49/month' as the wrong currency for Germany
Does not state a converted euro price without a sourced exchange rate and date
Flags '03/04/2026' as an ambiguous date and gives an unambiguous fix
Flags '1,000.50' and '10,000' for the German decimal and thousands separators
Presents the issues in a table with item, issue, market rule, and on-market fix columns

evals.prompt: Localize this for the UK: 'Optimize your organization's workflow with Brightline Analyzer. Customize every color and label, and hit a home run on your quarterly reporting.'
evals.expected_output: Changes US spellings to en-GB (optimise, organisation, customise, colour), keeps the product name 'Brightline Analyzer' unchanged, and flags the baseball idiom 'hit a home run'.
assertions: Changes 'optimize,' 'organization,' 'customize,' and 'color' to en-GB spellings
Keeps the product name 'Brightline Analyzer' unchanged
Flags 'hit a home run' as an idiom that may not land in the UK
Does not flag lines that are already fine

evals.prompt: Will this messaging work in Japan? 'Zenly Expense is the #1 expense app in America. Free forever, guaranteed savings on every trip.'
evals.expected_output: First-principles mode. Flags the '#1' superlative, 'free forever,' and 'guaranteed savings' against local advertising and claims rules, labeling each market rule Assumed or Gap rather than Sourced, with fallbacks for any claim it cannot verify.
assertions: States that no company canon was found and that it is checking from first principles
Flags '#1 expense app in America' as a superlative needing a source and as scoped to another market
Flags 'guaranteed savings' as an outcome claim
Flags 'free forever'
Labels each Japanese market rule Assumed or Gap unless it gives a citation
Gives a fallback line for any claim it marks as a Gap
